memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "What if there are fifty righteous people in the city? Will you really sweep it away and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous people in it?... Will not the Judge of all the earth do right?" - Gen 18:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Listen to the ground of Abraham's boldness: "Will not the Judge of all the earth do right?" He appeals not to his own worthiness, not to Sodom's merit, but to God's character. He essentially says, "God, You are just. Act according to who You are." This is prayer at its most confident - pleading God's own nature back to Him.

This is how we can pray with boldness. We do not come to God on the basis of what we deserve or what those we pray for deserve. We come on the basis of who God is - His justice, His mercy, His faithfulness, His love. When we pray, "Lord, You are merciful, so have mercy," we are praying like Abraham.

Notice too Abraham's remarkable idea: that God might "spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous people in it." He grasps something profound - that the presence of the righteous can hold back judgement, that a few faithful ones can be a blessing to many. Godly people are a preserving influence in a dark world.

This points forward to the gospel's heart. If the presence of righteous people could spare a city, how much more does the one perfectly Righteous One, Jesus, save all who are found in Him? He is the true "salt of the earth" (Matt 5:13) whose righteousness saves. Pray boldly today, appealing not to your merit but to the unchanging character of the God who always does right.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you pray based on what you deserve, or on who God is?
- How can you be a "preserving" godly influence where God has placed you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You are the Judge of all the earth who always does right. Teach me to pray boldly, appealing to Your character rather than my merit. Make me a preserving influence for good where You have placed me.
Amen.
